title: Forschungsprojektleiter:in Energiedaten & Gebäudetechnik (d/w/m)
descriptionHtml:
termios macht Heizen in Wohn- und Gewerbeimmobilien smarter und klimafreundlicher. Unser Thermostat spart spürbar Energie und hilft Asset Managern, Wohnungsunternehmen und Eigentümern, ihre ESG- und Net-Zero-Ziele zu erreichen.

termios ist ein 2023 gegründetes Joint-Venture von mantro als Company Builder, dem sauerländischen Familienunternehmen Oventrop und der Düsseldorfer LEG Immobilien SE. Als Technologieunternehmen entwickeln wir grüne Lösungen rund um Heizen, Nachhaltigkeit und ESG für Wohnimmobilien.

Warum wir diese Stelle besetzen

Unser Thermostat termios Pro übernimmt den hydraulischen Abgleich automatisch, für jeden einzelnen Heizkörper, und ist in tausenden Wohnungen verbaut. Daraus entsteht ein Messdatenbestand zum realen Heizbetrieb im Gebäudebestand, wie ihn kaum ein einzelnes Forschungsprojekt aufbauen kann.

Wie viel Energie spart der automatische Abgleich wirklich, unter welchen Bedingungen, und wie weist man das sauber nach? Diese und ähnliche Fragestellungen wollen wir gemeinsam mit Hochschulen, Forschungsinstituten, Wohnungsunternehmen und Fördergebern beantworten.

Du startest dabei nicht bei null: Wir haben bereits zwei vom BMWE geförderte Forschungsprojekte und sind in weiteren Forschungsfeldern aktiv. Für dieses wachsende Portfolio suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt jemanden, der Forschung nicht nur organisiert, sondern selbst betreibt.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Studiendesign und Feldversuche: Du übersetzt offene Fragen in prüfbare Hypothesen und ein belastbares Studiendesign mit Vergleichsgruppen, Baseline, Witterungsbereinigung und Messkonzept. Messkampagnen in realen Liegenschaften setzt du gemeinsam mit Field Service und Anlagentechnik um.

  • Datenanalyse: Du wertest Zeitreihen aus dem Gerätebestand und aus Messkampagnen selbst aus, quantifizierst Effekte und Unsicherheiten und trennst sauber zwischen Korrelation und Wirkung.

  • Ergebnisse: Du bereitest Erkenntnisse für Abschlussberichte, Fachpublikationen, Konferenzen und Kunden auf und sorgst dafür, dass sie in unsere Algorithmen und Produktentwicklung zurückfließen.

  • Projektleitung: Du steuerst mehrere parallel laufende Forschungs- und Pilotprojekte, von Arbeitspaketen und Meilensteinen über Budgets und Berichtspflichten bis zu Kooperationsverträgen, Datenschutz und Förderrichtlinien.

  • Förderung und Akquise: Du findest passende Förderprogramme auf Landes-, Bundes- und EU-Ebene, entwickelst Projektideen mit Partnern und schreibst Skizzen und Anträge.

Das bringst du mit

  • Studium: Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in einem ingenieur-, natur- oder datenwissenschaftlichen Fach, z. B. Gebäude- und Energietechnik, Versorgungstechnik, Bauphysik, Physik, Mathematik oder Informatik.

  • Forschungserfahrung: Du hast mehrere Jahre in der angewandten Forschung gearbeitet, etwa an einem Fraunhofer-Institut, einer anderen Forschungseinrichtung, einer Hochschule oder in einer F&E-Abteilung, idealerweise im Umfeld Gebäude, Energie oder TGA.

  • Methodik und Daten: Du hast Studien oder Messkampagnen selbst konzipiert und ausgewertet, wendest statistische Verfahren wie Regression, Zeitreihenanalyse und Hypothesentests sicher an und arbeitest dabei mit Python oder R sowie SQL.

  • Projektleitung: Du hast Projekte mit mehreren Partnern geleitet oder koordiniert und bringst unterschiedliche Interessen zusammen.

  • Kommunikation: Du schreibst klar und belastbar, vom Förderantrag bis zur Veröffentlichung. Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch und Englisch auf Arbeitsniveau.

Das ist ein Plus

Niemand bringt alles mit. Vieles davon lernst du bei uns.

  • Förderprojekte: Du hast schon Anträge geschrieben oder öffentlich geförderte Projekte abgewickelt.

  • Heizungstechnik: Du kennst dich mit Heizungshydraulik, hydraulischem Abgleich und Wärmeerzeugern wie Fernwärme oder Wärmepumpe aus.

  • Einsparnachweise: Du kennst Verfahren zur Messung und Verifikation von Einsparungen, z. B. IPMVP.

  • Modelle: Du hast Erfahrung mit Gebäudesimulation (z. B. Modelica, TRNSYS) oder Machine Learning.

  • Promotion oder eigene Publikationen

Gute Gründe, um bei uns durchzustarten

  • Forschung, die ankommt: Wenn du eine Hypothese an einem realen Gebäude prüfen willst, organisieren wir das. Was du herausfindest, landet im Produkt, und Veröffentlichungen sind ausdrücklich erwünscht.

  • Alles unter einem Dach: Hardware, Firmware, Funk, Cloud und Daten. Wer das gebaut hat, wonach du fragst, sitzt im selben Team.

  • Gestaltungsfreiraum ab dem ersten Tag, in einem agilen Team mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

  • Flexibilität: Du arbeitest hybrid in Düsseldorf oder München, mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten.

  • Konditionen: Unbefristete Festanstellung, wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung, 30 Tage Urlaub, Urban Sports und Corporate Benefits sowie regelmäßige Teamevents.

Klingt nach dir?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf, gern mit Publikationsliste oder Links zu deinen Projekten. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Schreib uns lieber ein paar Sätze dazu, welche Forschungsfrage dich bei uns besonders reizt.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Isembard

Isembard is rebuilding industrial capacity through a connected network of factories. We bring skilled people, advanced machine tools and our own software, MasonOS, together to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and robotics.

The role

This role sits where MasonOS meets the shop floor. Every new factory in our network adds training, adoption and support work. You will embed with factories and network sites, own their success with MasonOS end to end, ship production code, apply AI to their workflows and build the tools that make each new site easier than the last.

It is not a support role. It is a build role, deployed forward, defining a new function rather than filling a seat. You will be based at our London factory, with roughly 30 to 50 per cent of your time embedded at other sites. We are open to graduate and experienced engineers. The package includes equity.

  • Run onboarding, training and day-to-day adoption with machinists, engineers and site operators.

  • Turn repeated support questions into playbooks, training material or self-service tools. You are measured on the support burden falling, not on tickets closed.

  • Put agentic workflows into operational use: reporting, supplier follow-ups and order status.

  • Ship fixes and small features into MasonOS through the same review as every other engineer.

  • Turn patterns from the field into clear, written requirements for the roadmap.

What you bring

  • The ability to ship production code with minimal supervision.

  • Full-stack fluency across backend, frontend and integrations.

  • Hands-on experience applying LLMs to real workflows.

  • Clear communication with operators and technical leaders, and the ability to build trust on site.

  • The judgement to decide what matters without waiting for a ticket queue.

  • Useful, not essential: forward-deployed or deployment engineering experience, exposure to manufacturing, CNC, aerospace or defence, or MES or ERP systems.

title: Founding Customer Value Manager (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Intro

Die Bauindustrie verliert jährlich 1,6 Billionen USD durch Ineffizienzen. Einer der Hauptgründe: Dieselben Fehler wiederholen sich immer wieder, weil entscheidende Informationen noch immer in Papierdokumenten und unstrukturierten Dateien verborgen sind.

Genau hier setzt alago an. Wir sind ein Team von 15 Personen und entwickeln KI-gestütztes Projektmanagement für die Baubranche. Bereits heute vertrauen uns mehr als 40 Kunden. Unsere Vision ist es, Risiken in Bauprojekten frühzeitig sichtbar zu machen – damit Großprojekte nicht mehr Jahrzehnte dauern oder scheitern.

Wir haben letztes Jahr eine Pre-Seed-Finanzierung von über 1 Mio. € von führenden VCs der Baubranche sowie einem der größten Projektentwickler Deutschlands abgeschlossen.

75 % der Infrastruktur, die im Jahr 2050 existieren wird, ist heute noch nicht gebaut. Lasst uns sie von Anfang an richtig bauen.

Tasks

Customer Experience ist bei uns kein Support-Ticket-Job. Du besitzt den kompletten Kundenlebenszyklus nach dem Vertragsabschluss — kommerziell, operativ und im Produkt.

Damit sitzt du an der Stelle im Unternehmen, an der beide Seiten gleichzeitig sichtbar sind: Du weißt, was Kunden wirklich brauchen und wofür sie zahlen — und du weißt, was das Produkt kann und was es kosten würde, es zu können. Genau daraus entstehen die besten Produktentscheidungen und die besten Deals.

Du bist die erste Person in dieser Rolle und baust den Bereich so, wie er in zwei Jahren für dreißig Leute funktionieren muss.

💰 Revenue Ownership

  • Du besitzt einen Kundenstamm mit klarer Umsatzverantwortung: Retention, Expansion, Renewals.

  • Du erkennst, wo ein Kunde mehr Wert ziehen könnte, und machst den Upsell selbst – weitere Nutzer, weitere Projekte, weitere Produkte.

  • Du verhandelst Verlängerungen und Erweiterungen und führst sie bis zur Unterschrift.

🚀 Value Creation über den gesamten Kundenlebenszyklus

  • Du übernimmst den Kunden ab dem ersten Onboarding-Kontakt: Setup, Projektdaten, Konfiguration, Schulung der Teams.

  • Du führst den Rollout vom Pilotprojekt in die Fläche – und sorgst dafür, dass die Nutzung nicht nach vier Wochen einschläft.

  • Du machst Value Reviews mit messbaren Zahlen statt Höflichkeitsterminen und machst sichtbar, was alago dem Kunden konkret gebracht hat.

🛟 Customer Support

  • Du verantwortest unseren Support: Anfragen beantworten, priorisieren, Muster erkennen.

  • Du debuggst Customer Flows in der Software selbst – du reichst ein Problem nicht weiter, du reproduzierst es, grenzt es ein und beschreibst es so, dass es lösbar ist.

  • Du baust Doku, Self-Service und KI-gestützte Antworten so auf, dass dieselbe Frage nicht zehnmal auf deinem Tisch landet.

⚙️ Product Engine – du baust mit

  • Du löst selbst, was sich ohne Engineering lösen lässt: Konfiguration, Datenbereinigung, kleine Automatisierungen und Skripte – mit KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder n8n. Was Code im Kernprodukt braucht, übergibst du so präzise an unser Engineering-Team, dass es schnell gelöst ist.

  • Du verantwortest Integrationen und Datenimporte: Du scopst die Anbindung an Kundensysteme, prüfst, was machbar ist, und bringst Migrationen gemeinsam mit unserem Engineering-Team ins Ziel – damit ein Onboarding Stunden statt Tage dauert.

  • Du bist die Stimme des Kunden im Produktprozess: Du übersetzt, was Nutzer, Projektleitungen, IT und QM wirklich brauchen, in klare, priorisierte Produkt-Inputs – mit Belegen, nicht mit Bauchgefühl – und testest neue Releases aus Kundensicht, bevor sie live gehen.

🏗️ Den Bereich aufbauen

  • Du schreibst die Playbooks für Onboarding, Rollout, Support und Upsell – und automatisierst sie, wo immer es geht.

  • Du entwickelst und betreibst die KI-Agents und Automatisierungen, die Customer Experience bei uns skalierbar machen, statt den Bereich mit Köpfen zu vergrößern.

Requirements

Muss-Kriterien

  • Du hattest bereits direkten Kundenkontakt in einer verantwortlichen Rolle – du hast Kunden selbst geführt, nicht nur zugearbeitet

  • Du hast Umsatzverantwortung getragen oder Umsatz ausgebaut (Renewals, Upsells, Expansion, Abschlüsse) und kannst das mit Zahlen belegen

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau und sicheres Englisch

  • Standort München oder Bereitschaft, dauerhaft von hier aus zu arbeiten

Pluspunkte

  • Du hast selbst schon aktiv entwickelt – eigene Projekte, Skripte, Integrationen, ein Side Project, das tatsächlich läuft

  • Du hast schon mit Claude Code (oder vergleichbaren Coding-Agents) echte Sachen gebaut und weißt, wie weit man damit ohne Engineering-Team kommt

  • Du kennst Teile unseres Stacks (TypeScript, React, Supabase) schon aus eigenen Projekten

  • Du hast schon in der Baubranche gearbeitet oder hast einen engen Bezug zu ihr

  • Du hast bereits in einem schnell wachsenden Early-Stage-Startup gearbeitet und weißt, wie es sich anfühlt, wenn es noch kein Playbook gibt

  • Du hast schon einmal einen Bereich oder Prozess von null aufgebaut

Wie du arbeitest

  • AI-native: Du nutzt KI reflexhaft, nicht gelegentlich. Du hast eigene Agents, Automatisierungen oder Tools gebaut (n8n, Claude Code, Lovable o. Ä.), testest neue Modelle sofort und weißt, was taugt.

  • Systems Thinker: Du siehst das System hinter dem einzelnen Kunden. Beim zweiten Mal baust du den Prozess, der das manuelle Lösen überflüssig macht – und dokumentierst ihn für die nächste Person.

  • Technische Tiefe: Du prüfst Daten, verfolgst Flows, liest Logs und grenzt Probleme sauber ein – und behebst sie, wo es geht, selbst mit KI-Tools. Du bist in der Software zu Hause, nicht nur in der Präsentation darüber.

  • Umsetzung & Ownership: Du bringst Dinge zu Ende, ohne dass jemand nachfassen muss.

Wenn du dich nicht in jedem Punkt wiederfindest, aber überzeugt bist, dass du zu alago passt, bewirb dich trotzdem. Entscheidend sind dein Potenzial und deine Lernkurve.

Warum alago?

Du wirst einer der tragenden Pfeiler dieser Firma

  • Du bist die erste Person für Customer Experience und bestimmst Prozesse, Tools, Standards und Kennzahlen. Was du baust, bleibt.

  • Customer Experience ist einer von sechs, sieben Bereichen, die alago tragen – und du besitzt ihn.

  • Du sitzt am Tisch, wenn die Entscheidungen fallen, die die Firma prägen. Der Weg führt zum Head of Customer Experience mit eigenem Team.

Du entwickelst dich in eines der gefragtesten Profile überhaupt

  • KI-Unternehmen suchen händeringend Leute, die Kunde und Produkt zugleich beherrschen – bei Palantir heißt das Forward Deployed Engineer.

  • Du lernst, Vertrauen aufzubauen, schwierige Gespräche zu führen und Kunden über Monate zu messbarem Wert zu begleiten.

  • Ab Tag eins Zugriff auf unsere Codebasis, Pairing mit dem Engineering-Team und echte Code-Reviews. Wer beides kann, hat danach jede Tür offen.

Du baust deine eigene Marke – und vervielfachst deinen Marktwert

  • Du begleitest unser Wachstum von 16 auf 30 Mitarbeitende in zwei Jahren.

  • Du knackst den Code, wie Onboarding, Rollout, Support und Upsell vorhersehbar und wiederholbar werden – und nimmst dieses Playbook überallhin mit.

Du beschleunigst deine Entwicklung

  • Ob eigene Gründung oder Head of Customer Experience: Halbjährliche Performance-Reviews, konkrete Entwicklungsschritte alle ~9 Monate.

  • Wöchentliche Trainings, erfahrene Coaches und Mentor:innen und eine umfangreiche Bibliothek.

Arbeite direkt mit den Foundern

  • Tag für Tag mit Janick (Go-to-Market & Strategy) und Ann-Christin (Product & Domain).

  • Frühe Phase heißt: viel Eigenverantwortung, kurze Feedback-Zyklen und die Freiheit, in die Rolle zu wachsen, die zu deinen Stärken passt.

Zusätzlich

  • Wellpass, zweimal pro Woche Team-Dinner und Unterstützung beim Relocation-Prozess.

  • Arbeitsplatz im WERK1, einem der aktivsten Startup-Hubs Münchens.

Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Bewerbung

  2. Erstgespräch (30 Minuten)

  3. Deep-Dive mit einem Founder (40 Minuten)

  4. Case Study (halber Tag vor Ort in München) – z. B. ein hängendes Rollout retten, einen Upsell-Case rechnen oder einen Customer Flow im Produkt debuggen

  5. Entscheidung – Rückmeldung innerhalb von 24 Stunden. Wenn es für beide Seiten passt – freuen wir uns sehr auf die Zusammenarbeit! 🎉

title: Founding Operations & Systems Lead
descriptionHtml:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

 

Why we're hiring

  • We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.

  • This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.

  • We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

  • Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

  • The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

  • We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

  • Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.

  • The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.

  • We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

     

What you'll own

  • Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.

  • Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.

  • Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.

  • Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.

  • The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.

     

What we're looking for

  • You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.

  • Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.

  • Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
    A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

  • In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

  • Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

  • Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.

     

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up
    Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed
    We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership
    Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty
    If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service
    Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

     

This role is probably not for you if

  • You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;

  • You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

  • You are risk-averse;

  • You want a 9-5;

  • You take yourself too seriously;

  • You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

     

Salary

£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

 

Hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. A call with our Head of People, an in-person session with the founders where you solve a real Odin problem end to end with AI, then a final with the founders. The last two can run on the same day.

 

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

 

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

  • Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

title: Founding Strategy and Operations Analyst role

When things go wrong, insurance has one job: get people and businesses back on their feet. Too often, it doesn't. At ClaimSorted, we're changing that, and building a more resilient world where people and businesses have the confidence to go after bigger opportunities.

We're creating the company that will define how claims are handled for the next generation. The world's largest insurers and Fortune 500 companies already trust us to handle their claims and manage their risk.

And we're moving fast. We grew 10x in the past year, raised one of the largest InsurTech rounds of its kind, and are backed by Y Combinator, Atomico and Eurazeo. We ship, learn and improve every week, never settling for "how it's always been done."

We're just getting started. There's never been a better time to join.

The Role

Handling claims at scale requires a strong operational foundation. Qualifications

  • Strong written and spoken communication, with a proven ability to work cross-functionally

  • A generalist mindset: comfortable picking up whatever problem matters most and moving quickly

Our Values

  • Move Fast – Act decisively, iterate quickly, optimise for momentum.

title: Global PR Operations Lead - 12 month FTC
descriptionHtml:
About Skyscanner

Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻.

Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍.

Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here).

Now, we’re on the lookout for a Global PR Lead to help us bring that vision to even more travellers.

About the role
(Hybrid)

This is a role at the heart of our fast-paced, high-volume PR team, helping keep our communications flying in formation across 23 markets worldwide. You’ll be the central point connecting plans, people, budgets, agencies and operations — making sure our global PR machine runs smoothly, efficiently and at scale.

Working closely with our Senior Director of Communications, regional PR leads, internal teams and global agency partners, you’ll help turn our international PR strategy into coordinated action. From shaping global initiatives to sharpening the way we plan, measure and operate, you’ll bring the structure that helps brilliant PR ideas travel further.

What you’ll be doing

  • Driving global PR planning: You’ll lead the planning process with our global PR agency hub, partnering with the Senior Director of Communications to keep forecasting, budgets, resources and priorities aligned.

  • Turning measurement into momentum: You’ll work closely with our measurement lead to make sure reporting is accurate, useful and connected to the strategies and decisions that matter.

  • Optimising our PR ecosystem: You’ll partner with Procurement and Finance to make sure we have the right suppliers, commercial setup and financial tracking in place to support growth — without the spreadsheet drama.

  • Keeping priorities moving: You’ll traffic-manage inbound requests, help the team navigate competing priorities and make sure resources are focused where they can have the greatest impact.

  • Leading global PR initiatives: You’ll spearhead strategic PR initiatives and special projects beyond our core campaigns, while supporting the delivery of our Awareness strategy and Big Bet activity through PR.

  • Making operations smarter: You’ll lead and collaborate on cross-functional improvements spanning tools and technology, including Tableau, ThoughtSpot, AI and our Product Ops model — finding smarter ways for a global team to work at scale.

  • Creating consistency across markets: You’ll partner with market leads, our global agency hub and Corporate and B2B PR teams to develop playbooks, strengthen processes and drive consistent adoption and delivery across 23 markets. You’ll also manage and develop our PR Coordinator, keeping calendars, finance trackers and reporting firmly on course.

About you

  • Global PR operator: You’ve worked in complex, international communications environments and know how to turn lots of moving parts into one joined-up plan.

  • Strategic and operational: You’re equally comfortable shaping a global PR initiative and getting into the detail needed to make it happen. Big picture, meet beautifully organised spreadsheet.

  • Stakeholder savvy: You build trusted relationships across senior leaders, market teams, agencies and cross-functional partners, bringing people together around shared priorities.

  • Agency confident: You know how to get the best from global agency relationships, balancing clear direction, strong partnership and accountability for delivery.

  • Commercially switched-on: You’re comfortable working with budgets, forecasting, suppliers, Procurement and Finance, and you understand how strong operational foundations help teams achieve more.

  • Tech and data curious: You’re interested in how measurement, dashboards, AI and smarter tools can improve PR operations, reporting and decision-making at scale.

  • Calm in the whirlwind: You thrive in fast-paced environments, can prioritise when everything feels important, and enjoy helping teams work more effectively. You’re also comfortable managing and developing others along the way.


What it's like here

We are the real deal - no corporate gloss, no empty promises. Just a team of genuinely curious, caring humans ❤️, building things that help travellers explore the world a little easier 🧭.

Skyscanner is made up of brilliant humans from every corner of the world. We believe travel makes the world better - and that the same is true of our diverse teams. We're proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and products that are accessible to all ✨.

Sound like your kind of adventure? 🚀 Apply now and help us shape the future of travel.

We're committed to ensuring our application and recruitment processes are inclusive and accessible to everyone. If you require any reasonable adjustments or accommodations for interviews, and/or wish to apply under the Disability Confident scheme, please let your recruiter know. If you’d like more information on any of our policies, such as hybrid working or Parental Leave policies (typically we pay a minimum of 24 weeks birth parent/maternity leave globally), our recruitment team can provide more information on these.

title: Go-To-Market Specialist
descriptionHtml:

Private Equity Insights is the world’s largest Private Equity community with 1m PE professionals, delivering impact through 12 global PE conferences with thousands of the world’s best investors and operators such as Blackstone, BlackRock, Apollo, Carlyle, CVC, KKR, and many more.

  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue

Role is full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week.

What you can bring

title: Head of backend
descriptionHtml:
About SchemeServe

SchemeServe is insurance software like no other.

Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support.

Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values.

We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats.

We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it.

We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post.

We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work.

If you're excited, good! So are we.

Come and join the Insurtech revolution!

Principal Backend Engineer

UK Remote

We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better.

You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction.

But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design.

Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software.

You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement.

What We Mean By Principal



This is a deeply technical role.

You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers.

But technical knowledge alone isn't enough.

We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software.

Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments.

We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us.

That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs.

Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology.

Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have.

Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution.

We're quite comfortable with that.

How You'll Lead



Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority.

We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with:

"We'd better ask the Principal Engineer."

If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own.

Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience.

And be prepared to change your own mind too.

The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one.

Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you.

You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team.

But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded.

The Technical Challenge



Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years.

At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services.

Our backend estate includes:


  • .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET.
  • TypeScript services.
  • Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis.
  • Azure cloud infrastructure.
  • Cloudflare platform services.
  • API-first architecture.
  • Git-based development workflows.


We're continuing to modernise, but we're not interested in modernisation for modernisation's sake.

We aren't trying to win an award for having the most fashionable architecture diagram.

We want a secure, reliable and maintainable platform that can support SchemeServe for many years to come – and we want you to help us decide what should evolve and, just as importantly, what doesn't need changing.

What You'll Do



You'll work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to:


  • Shape our backend engineering strategy, architecture and technical direction.
  • Help engineers make better technical and architectural decisions.
  • Develop sensible engineering principles and guardrails without replacing good judgement with rules.
  • Guide the continued evolution of our monolith and modern service-based platform.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, developing their technical skills and judgement.
  • Review significant designs and architectural decisions and challenge unnecessary complexity.
  • Champion security, quality, testing, observability, resilience and performance.
  • Identify technical risks and help teams navigate them.
  • Evaluate technologies and patterns based on their value to SchemeServe rather than their popularity elsewhere.
  • Balance long-term engineering quality with short-term business needs.
  • Occasionally contribute directly to implementation when that's genuinely the best way to help.
  • Be a generally awesome person.


What We're Looking For



You'll need:


  • Deep expertise in modern backend engineering and strong commercial C#/.NET experience.
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture, distributed systems and API design.
  • Experience with mature legacy applications and modern service-oriented architectures.
  • Strong cloud architecture experience, ideally Azure.
  • Excellent understanding of databases, security, testing, maintainability and modern software delivery.
  • Experience shaping engineering principles and practices across teams.
  • A track record of making engineers around you better through mentoring, coaching and technical leadership.
  • The ability to challenge experienced engineers constructively without becoming a gatekeeper.
  • Strong opinions, loosely held – the confidence to challenge and the humility to change your mind.
  • Excellent communication and the ability to influence without relying on authority.
  • Excellent technical judgement, balancing quality, complexity, risk, cost and business value.


Most importantly, we're looking for someone who asks:

"What's the right solution for us?"

rather than:

"What's the way everyone else is doing it?"

Nice To Have


  • Experience modernising large monolithic applications.
  • Commercial TypeScript backend experience.
  • Cloudflare or edge technology experience.
  • SaaS platforms at scale.
  • Financial services, insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Observability, platform engineering or SRE experience.
  • AI-assisted development and engineering productivity tooling.


You don't need to tick every box.

If you've got the technical depth, judgement and ability to make engineers around you better, we'd rather have a conversation than lose a great candidate because you haven't used one particular technology.

What Success Looks Like



Within your first year:


  • Engineers are making stronger technical and architectural decisions with greater confidence.
  • Our engineering principles are understood rather than blindly followed.
  • Technical discussions are constructive, pragmatic and result in clear decisions.
  • Security, reliability, maintainability and performance concerns are identified earlier.

title: Head of Financial Controller
descriptionHtml:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

As Head of Financial Controller, you will own the full accounting function across Filigran's entities, including revenue recognition, consolidation, monthly and year-end close, and internal controls. You will report directly to the VP of Finance. The team is small so this role demands both strategic ownership and significant hands-on execution.

Systems & Scalability

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

title: Head of Talent
descriptionHtml:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

About the role: hire the best, fast

As Head of Talent Acquisition, you own how Andercore hires: from the hiring plan to the signed contract, across engineering, product, data, commercial and operations. You report to the CEO and work closely with every member of the leadership team.

We are growing fast, and in a small team every hire changes what the company can do. Today, hiring runs through our hiring managers, a few search partners and a lot of individual effort. What we don't have yet is a repeatable system that consistently finds exceptional people, especially the driven, curious builders who rarely apply through standard channels.

Your job is to build that talent engine: direct sourcing, an employer brand that reaches the right people, a structured and fast process, and search partners that deliver. You go deep on every critical search yourself, try new channels and formats, and make the whole function AI-native, so a small talent team can hire at the pace of a scale-up.

What you will do: build the talent engine

01 Hiring plan and strategy

  • Translate the company plan into a hiring plan with leadership, and prioritise the roles that matter most.

  • Own headcount forecasting together with Finance.

  • Report on pipeline health, speed and quality, and act on what the numbers show.

02 Direct sourcing and employer brand

  • Build in-house sourcing so most hires come directly or through referrals.

  • Tell Andercore's story where builders are: events, communities, content and our own team.

  • Set up a referral programme that our people actually use.

03 A structured, fast process

  • Define interview loops, scorecards and hiring committees with leadership, and train hiring managers to use them.

  • Keep time-to-offer short without lowering the bar.

  • Make the candidate experience excellent, from scheduling to feedback.

04 Search partners

  • Select and manage search partners on clear terms, and brief them sharply.

  • Hold them to quality, and use executive search only where it pays off.

05 AI-native recruiting

  • Use AI and our applicant tracking system to automate screening, outreach, scheduling and reporting.

  • Run recruiting on data: funnel conversion, source quality and time-to-hire.

06 Lead and close

  • Build and lead the talent team.

  • Own the most critical searches yourself, including leadership roles, and close offers with candidates and hiring managers.

What success looks like: great people, hired fast

  • Critical roles filled with people who raise the bar, on time

  • Most hires through direct sourcing and referrals, with lower agency spend

  • Short time-to-offer and a high offer acceptance rate

  • Hiring managers use consistent scorecards and calibrate together

  • Candidates, including those we turn down, would recommend our process

  • A steady pipeline of driven builders for engineering, commercial and leadership roles

What you bring: you've built a talent engine, now build ours

  1. A proven track record leading talent acquisition in a fast-growing startup or scale-up, hiring across tech and commercial roles.

  2. Hands-on experience sourcing and closing senior and leadership hires yourself, including engineering leaders.

  3. Experience building talent acquisition from scratch or rebuilding it: process, tooling, scorecards, employer brand and team.

  4. Strong sourcing craft: you find people who are not looking, especially engineers and builders.

  5. A data-driven way of working: funnel metrics, forecasting and clear reporting to leadership.

  6. Curiosity and drive: you try new channels, formats and tools, and you go deep until something works.

  7. An AI-native way of working: you use AI to automate the repetitive parts of recruiting.

  8. Fluent English. German, and knowledge of the Berlin tech market and German hiring practice, are a plus.

The role

You will check whether a company has the legal right to use the health data its business depends on, as part of technology due diligence for clients who are selling, buying or investing in data and AI companies. Buyers in life sciences want to know that client data is handled lawfully, deleted when it should be, and not used for anything the contracts do not allow.

You report to an Intelance engagement partner and work with our technology due diligence lead, who brings your findings into the final report.

What you will do

  • Confirm who is the controller and who is the processor for each type of data, and check the data processing agreements in place.

  • Review client contracts to see whether client data may be used to improve AI workflows, test suites or models.

  • Check how data is deleted when contracts end, and whether that is possible where data has shaped models or tests.

  • Review licences for real world data from third party providers, and what happens to them if the company changes owner.

  • Check data transfers outside the UK, including any use of outside AI providers.

  • Check HIPAA readiness where US health data is involved.

  • Rate each finding by how it could affect the deal, and write clear, practical fixes.

What you will bring

  • At least five years advising on data protection in health, pharmaceutical or life sciences settings.

  • Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR and international data transfers. HIPAA knowledge is a strong plus.

  • Experience reviewing data processing agreements and data licences.

  • A recognised qualification such as CIPP/E or the BCS Practitioner Certificate, or legal practice in data protection.

  • Clear, plain writing that founders, buyers and lawyers can follow.

  • Experience of AI and data rights, or of due diligence work, is a strong plus.

How the work is set up

  • Remote within the UK, with occasional meetings in London.

  • Around 3 to 5 days between late November 2026 and the end of January 2027, with further engagements as the practice grows.

  • Freelance, or through your own limited company, at £450 to £600 a day depending on experience. Reasonable travel costs for client meetings are covered.

  • A panel agreement, NDA and statement of work are signed before any client details are shared.

  • You work from an Intelance mailbox and use our evidence log and report templates, so every report meets the same standard.

How to apply

Send your CV and answer the short screening questions. They take about two minutes. We aim to reply to every shortlisted candidate within five working days.

title: Infrastructure Software Engineering – Platform & Build
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The Role

As an Infrastructure Platform Engineer you will be a core part of our technical team working alongside the hardware, software and research teams to solve cutting-edge problems in AI hardware, ranging from verification to simulation, alongside the best of the best (DeepMind, Apple, Meta…).

About the Software organisation at Fractile

Infrastructure sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing.

About the team and role

The Infrastructure team is responsible for the core platform and systems at Fractile. We build, scale, and optimize the mission-critical systems that power our entire engineering org, including our multi-language Bazel monorepo and CI pipelines. From hardware design and verification to kernel development and ML compilers, we enable all Fractile engineers to ship fast and reliably.

The team brings both deep build system expertise and an SRE mindset: reliability, build performance, debugging CI failures systematically, and giving the engineering organisation clear visibility into how our infrastructure is performing.

As an Infrastructure Platform Engineer, you will:

  • Own the CI infrastructure end-to-end: create, maintain and debug reproducible multi-language CI pipelines, and optimize CI performance across large compute clusters.

  • Build and maintain infrastructure observability, alerting, runbooks, and incident response workflows for Fractile's infrastructure.

  • Own our infrastructure as code, automating provisioning of hybrid cloud and on-prem resources from a single source of truth.

  • Scale and maintain Fractile's Bazel monorepo as we continue growing across Python, C++, Rust, SystemVerilog, and ML workloads.

  • Shape the infrastructure and platform experience for every engineer at Fractile.

About you

You bring deep infrastructure and build systems expertise alongside an SRE mindset. You are systematic in how you approach fault isolation and root cause analysis, and you apply metrics-driven thinking to build reliability and developer productivity. You thrive on variety (ML, compilers, kernel drivers, simulators, hardware verification) and you understand that your work becomes the foundation every engineer at Fractile builds on. You take that responsibility seriously.

Key Requirements

  • 5+ years in software, platform, or infrastructure engineering

  • 5+ years hands-on experience working with CI/CD for large-scale products, including monitoring, debugging performance and resolving pipeline failures at scale

  • 3+ years working with build systems, preferably modern cross-language build systems with an emphasis on correctness, high performance and extensibility, such as Bazel, Buck, Pants, Please, etc.

  • Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform / OpenTofu, or Pulumi)

  • Experience with monitoring and observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, or similar)

  • Working knowledge and practice of DevOps / SRE principles: SLOs, alerting design, incident management, and on-call practice

  • Strong proficiency in at least one systems or scripting language used for tooling (Python preferred; Go or Rust also relevant), with a track record of shipping well-tested, maintainable developer tooling that other engineers rely on: CLIs, CI integrations, build and release automation

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us!

title: Innovative Project Planner (Data Centres / Buildings / High-tech / Infrastructure) - UK (Hybrid)
descriptionHtml:
Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. ____________________________________________________________ We are Laminar Projects! If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.) We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.) The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.) This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. (Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.) Core values for a good life A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has: - Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself - Care about people – your relationship with others around you - Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team - Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world We enshrined our values in our vision: We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that: - Connects us with meaningful relationships - Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans - Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world. And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions: - To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation - To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society ____________________________________________________________ The Role Purpose of the role You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. Your team This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on: - Understanding what the real problems of projects are - Implementing the best solutions to those problems - Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors. Your top three objectives 1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 3. To develop yourself and everyone around you Your top five responsibilities 1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 4. Make scalable solutions: Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well You must have: - A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data - Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach - Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them - Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: - You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge - You like to be the smartest person in the room - You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback - You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team ____________________________________________________________ Frequently Asked Questions What kinds of projects would I be working on? It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres, infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects. These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. (Check out our case stories.) Who are our clients? Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. Where would I be working? One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. ____________________________________________________________ Benefits The standard stuff: - Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage – for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority - Pension Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future – with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance - Professional body membership. One fee covered per year – so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft - Cycle to Work Scheme. A tax-efficient way to get wheels – and do your bit for the environment The life-changing stuff: - In-house coaching. Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally – professionally and as a human being - Equity upside. As we grow, you grow. Our generous equity scheme is especially powerful for those who stay with us on our journey. You help us build the future – and own a piece of it - Flexible working. Work where it makes sense – most of our team works from home, visiting sites or clients regularly. We care about outcomes, not clock-ins - Relentless development. Our goal is for every year here to be worth five years of development anywhere else. You’ll get a coach, a mentor, honest feedback, and a culture that challenges you to keep levelling up ____________________________________________________________ Important! Applying properly We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining: - Why you want to join us - What you’ll bring to the team We aren't a giant, faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team, so your letter will be read carefully. After that, we’ll reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you get to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself. A couple of technical and personal assessments follow to understand your capability based on our own development matrix. This is to ensure that when you join, you’re starting at the right level of responsibility.

title: Insurance Product Manager / Underwriter (P&C)
descriptionHtml:
Most insurance product roles ask you to perfect one product in one market. This one asks you to build Europe’s SME insurance products: decide what we cover and who we insure, negotiate it with our carriers and get it live, market after market.

Deep in the wording. Fast in the build.

About Insify

Insurance for entrepreneurs is still built the old way: one market at a time, wordings nobody reads, and cover that leaves out the very businesses that need it most.

We're doing it differently.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France, Germany and Ireland, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.


What you’ll own in your first year

You won’t inherit a finished product shelf. You’ll build the engine that fills it.

  1. Build the product engine. Turn how we benchmark a market into a system: compare cover, limits and exclusions across local players, our Dutch home product and our other markets, so every new product starts from facts, not gut feeling.
  2. Make the call on cover. Decide what we cover, what we don’t and who we insure, and turn it into a proposal. The tools do the comparison; the judgment is yours.
  3. Get it signed. Take the proposal to our risk carriers and negotiate it. You know what to push on, what to let go and which clause will set off six red flags.
  4. Get it live. Adapt our wordings to each new market, run the legal review and launch. Less writing from scratch, more making one strong product fit the next market. Then track loss ratios, competition and customer feedback, and sharpen it.
  5. Build what doesn’t exist yet. In the markets where we double down, own custom products from the insurance side, including cover for the trades and businesses others decline.

Who you are

You’re an insurance expert first and a builder second, but a real one.

  • You have 5+ years hands-on in commercial P&C (Property & Casualty) at an insurer, MGA, (re)insurer or specialist broker, across underwriting, product and wordings, ideally for SMEs.
  • You know what is covered, what isn’t and what should be. Hand you a wording from a market you’ve never worked in and you’ll spot the gaps within minutes.
  • You’ve worked across more than one line, product or market, and you can apply what you know to a market you’ve never seen.
  • You’ve sat at the table with insurers or capacity providers and know where the red lines are.
  • You’d rather fix insurance than complain about it. Maybe you already tried: at an insurtech, an MGA, your own startup, or on the carrier side building products with insurtechs.
  • You think like the customer: plain questions, fair cover, and no excluding everything just to be safe.
  • You’re at home in Excel and data, and curious about what automation and LLMs can take off your plate. You don’t need to code; our product and tech teams build the digital journey with you.
  • You work fluently in English; German, French or Dutch is a big plus.

    • What we offer
  • Real ownership. You decide what we cover and work directly with the MT, close to where decisions get made.
  • Range. More products and markets in a year than most people see in a decade at an incumbent.
  • A share in what we build. Equity, so you share in the value you build.
  • A team that cares. We live by four values: Grit, Care, Impact and Entrepreneurship.
  • Growth. Room to grow into leading our insurance product work as we add markets, plus an in-house coaching and leadership program.
  • The package. Competitive salary package + 6% pension, holidays, well-being budget and rich social events (ski trip, summer and winter party).
  • The basics, done well. Office in central Amsterdam, laptop, hybrid working. Relocation support.

    • If you know insurance inside out and you’d rather build products than maintain them, we’d like to meet you. No cover letter needed.

descriptionHtml:

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

About the Role

As a Junior Data Platform Engineer, you'll work alongside senior team members to tackle complex challenges, while taking ownership of your own areas of the problem, in a fast-paced environment where no two days look the same. The role is fundamentally about problem solving: understanding business challenges, breaking them down, and delivering pragmatic, scalable solutions.

You’ll work closely with product, analytics, and engineering teams, operating with a high degree of autonomy. That means proactively gathering context, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring work lands effectively.

Data Platform sits at the centre of the business, with a real opportunity to shape how teams interact with data. The focus is on enabling fast, iterative analytics, moving from idea to insight quickly, while maintaining strong foundations around reliability, cost, and security.

Our Modern Tech Stack

You’ll work across a broad set of technologies as we evolve the platform. Experience is helpful, but not essential:

  • Languages: Python, SQL, Terragrunt, JavaScript

  • Cloud: AWS (primary), some GCP

  • Warehouse & Storage: Snowflake, S3/Parquet

  • Data & ETL: dbt, Fivetran

  • Platform & Infra: Kubernetes, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Argo, GitHub Actions, HashiCorp Vault

  • Observability: Datadog, Grafana

  • Dashboarding: Preset

  • Other: Claude

What we’re looking for

Strong fundamentals and the ability to apply them pragmatically:

  • Solid programming ability (Python or similar)

  • Strong experience with Snowflake (or similar warehouses)

  • Good understanding of software engineering patterns and architectures

  • Experience building data-intensive systems

  • Cloud experience (AWS preferred)

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform ideally)

  • CI/CD best practices

  • Familiarity with modern data architectures (Lambda/Kappa)

Just as importantly, how you work:

  • A self-starter who takes ownership and drives work forward

  • Strong problem solver who focuses on understanding before building

  • Good judgement on build vs buy decisions

  • Comfortable working in ambiguity and shaping direction

  • Clear communicator across technical and non-technical audiences

  • Able to manage multiple streams of work without losing momentum

  • Pragmatic, balancing speed with scalability and reliability

  • Actively looks to improve ways of working, including leveraging AI tooling

Interview process

  • Initial call with Talent team

  • Hiring manager call

  • Technical interview

  • Final interview with VP of Platform

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites
